clue.text: Drink Scotsman knocked back in the college grounds

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is downed, but here the two pieces together are read from right to left

parts.note: to sup is to drink
Mac is the crossword's stock Scotsman, from the common surname prefix

explanation.surface: A Scotsman downs his drink on the university lawns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' turns the whole run SUPMAC round, giving the answer; 'knocked back' looks like drinking, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The grounds and buildings of a university or college are called its campus.

clue.text: Spanish uncle is seen in general uproar

indicators.note: the relative appears inside the other word

parts.note: common means general, shared by all
tio is Spanish for uncle

explanation.surface: A Spanish uncle turns up amid widespread uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is seen in' puts TIO inside COMMON, before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Commotion is noisy disturbance and confusion.

clue.text: Is of importance in these affairs

definitions.meaning: to matter is to be significant

explanation.surface: A remark on what counts in these dealings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both is significant and things that concern one.

clue.text: Nurse Lysit, oddly, is unlike her superior

indicators.note: behaving oddly, the letters of the nurse's name are jumbled

explanation.surface: Nurse Lysit behaves strangely, quite unlike her senior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' rearranges NURSELYSIT. A British nurse's superior on a ward is a sister, so being unlike her is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: In a British hospital a nurse's ward superior is the Sister, so not like her is sister-less in manner.

clue.text: Relating to land-Niagara River development

indicators.note: a development reworks the letters of the river's name plus R into a new order

explanation.surface: A geography note on how the land around the Niagara River was developed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development' rearranges NIAGARAR (Niagara plus R) into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrarian describes matters of farmland and its ownership or cultivation.

clue.text: They collect poor rags around yonder

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the other word
poor means in bad shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: yonder means over there

explanation.surface: Collectors gather tatty rags from over there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' turns RAGS into GARS, which goes 'around' THERE: GA-THERE-RS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gatherers are people who collect or pick things up.

clue.text: Eager for opera star's return

indicators.note: a return here is the singer's title running backwards

parts.note: a diva is a leading opera singer

explanation.surface: Fans are eager for a soprano's comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reads DIVA backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means keen or eager.

clue.text: They give us a tune if pressed

definitions.text: They give us a tune if pressed

parts.words: They give us a tune if pressed
parts.note: piano keys, once made of elephant tusk, play notes when pushed down

explanation.surface: Performers who sing only if urged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if pressed' sounds like reluctance, but piano keys literally sound when pressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano keys were traditionally made of elephant tusk, hence the slang name.

clue.text: Foul in 27 style

indicators.note: in signals that the answer is found within the following words

parts.note: 27 stands for the answer to clue 27 across, the Sicilian port

explanation.surface: Something foul done in a cross-referenced style.
explanation.walkthrough: Write out 27 across followed by 'style': the answer sits across the join.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty means unpleasant and offensive, like something foul.

clue.text: Helen her daughter is in the meadow

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits inside the word for field

parts.note: a lea is a meadow

explanation.surface: Helen's daughter is out in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'Helen her daughter', the mother of whom Helen is a daughter; in myth Leda was mother of Helen of Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Leda, visited by Zeus as a swan, bore Helen of Troy.

clue.text: First officer investing one ship's artist

indicators.note: to invest is to surround or besiege, so the officer's title encloses the other letters

parts.note: the mate is the first officer on a merchant ship
I is the Roman numeral for one
SS, steamship, is the standard prefix for a ship's name

explanation.surface: A ship's first officer puts money into an artist's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing' means besieging, not putting up money: MATE wraps round ISS.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French painter, a leader of the Fauves.

clue.text: A fitting job theirs, I see, among seamen

indicators.note: placed among means set in the middle of the sailors' word

parts.note: tars is an old word for sailors
lo is an archaic exclamation meaning look or see

explanation.surface: Sailors remark on a job that suits them well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts I and LO inside TARS. The definition is cryptic: tailors make clothes fit, so a fitting is their job.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes-makers hold fittings for customers, so fitting garments is their trade.

clue.text: Exaggerated condition in Dover perhaps

indicators.note: one word is set inside the other, the port's letters forming the outside
perhaps signals that the port's letters may be arranged differently

parts.note: a state is a condition, as in a state of health

explanation.surface: Someone claims the condition of the Kent port was exaggerated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges DOVER as OVERD, and 'in' puts STATE inside it, before the D. Dover is a Channel port in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstate something is to make it sound bigger than it is, so overstated means made too much of.

clue.text: Flower from Jersey

parts.note: a bloom from the Channel island, and also the nickname of the actress Lillie Langtry

explanation.surface: A blossom grown on Jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: Lillie Langtry, the Victorian actress born on Jersey (a Channel Island), was nicknamed after a white flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The flower is a bulb plant with trumpet blooms, and it gave the Jersey-born actress her nickname.

clue.text: Dearth of views about type of light on the pole

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other
the views go about, that is around, the light

parts.note: scenes are views
an arc light is a powerful electric lamp
S is the south pole

explanation.surface: A shortage of views of the aurora at the pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ARC inside SCENES, and 'on' sets that on S, south.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarceness is shortage, a dearth of something.

clue.text: Alternatively sent aid for reconstruction

indicators.note: the letters are to be rebuilt in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An aid package is dispatched to help rebuild somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for reconstruction' rearranges SENTAID into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words offer a substitute or other option: in place of that.

clue.text: Aids to sleep, unfortunately, may annoy

indicators.note: unfortunately means things went wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sleeping pills may sadly irritate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges AIDSSLEEP; 'to' and 'may' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Displease means to irritate or offend.

clue.text: Cuts out taxis, do you say ?

definitions.meaning: to excise is to cut out surgically

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether taxis are being dropped from a service.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is heard: 'taxis' said aloud is taxes, and excise is a tax on goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Excise means both to remove by cutting and a duty charged on goods.

clue.text: Author shows way to curtail service

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: to curtail is to cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: evensong is the evening church service

explanation.surface: A writer shows a way to shorten a service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to curtail' cuts the last letter G from EVENSONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson wrote Treasure Island.

clue.text: Sharpest of rocks ?

parts.note: pointed chalk stacks off the Isle of Wight, named for their sharpness, as sewing points are the sharpest objects

explanation.surface: A question about which rocks are the most pointed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Needles are a row of chalk stacks off the Isle of Wight, on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewing points are notoriously sharp, and the famous Isle of Wight rocks share their name.

clue.text: Reveals former positions

parts.note: ex means former
poses are positions held

explanation.surface: Uncovers postures held in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposes means uncovers or brings to light.

clue.text: Come up, Joseph, in drama school

definitions.meaning: to rise from beneath water to the top
Joseph is the hypocritical brother in Sheridan's play The School for Scandal

explanation.surface: Joseph is told to step up at drama school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drama school' is not an academy but Sheridan's comedy The School for Scandal, whose Joseph and Charles are brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: A diver rising to the top of water emerges there, and Joseph is a character in Sheridan's comedy.

clue.text: Shellfish at a French dance after midnight

parts.note: bal is French for dance or ball
one o'clock comes after midnight

explanation.surface: Shellfish served at a French ball in the small hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after midnight' gives ONE, the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Abalone is an edible sea snail with a shell lined with mother-of-pearl.

clue.text: But not the author of Great Expectations "

definitions.text: But not the author of Great Expectations

parts.words: But not the author of Great Expectations
parts.note: a great expectation is a strong wish, and Anthony ... wrote novels, but not the Dickens one

explanation.surface: A remark on someone who did not write the Dickens novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Great Expectations is by Dickens; the answer is both a great expectation and the surname of Anthony Hope, author of The Prisoner of Zenda.
explanation.definitionFit: A wish or expectation of something good, and also the surname of a different novelist.

clue.text: Top noise, American, in en richment of soil

parts.note: a spinning humming top hums
US is short for United States, so American

explanation.surface: Noise from an American top in fertilised soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' is the spinning toy, whose noise is a hum.
explanation.definitionFit: Humus is rotted organic matter that enriches soil.

clue.text: Everybody repeat, say, " Sister Susie's sewing shirts '

parts.note: all means everybody
to iterate is to repeat

explanation.surface: A class is told to recite a tongue-twister together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sister Susie's sewing shirts' is an example of the device, every word beginning with S; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Starting neighbouring words with the same sound, as in the tongue-twister, is what the verb means.

clue.text: Bismarck's bloody companion

parts.note: Bismarck said Germany would be united by blood and a certain metal, the companion of blood in his phrase

explanation.surface: A grim friend of the Prussian chancellor.
explanation.walkthrough: Bismarck's 1862 speech said great questions would be decided by 'blood and' this metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal paired with blood in Bismarck's famous phrase about German unity.

clue.text: Take communal meals in a Sicilian resort

parts.note: to mess is to eat together, as in a military mess

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers eat together in a resort on Sicily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' looks like a link, but it supplies the last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Messina is a port city in north-eastern Sicily.

clue.text: Burdensome blow is nothing to us

parts.note: a oner is a heavy single blow, British slang
O looks like zero, so it means nothing
us is taken as written

explanation.surface: A heavy blow means nothing to us.
explanation.walkthrough: A oner is old British slang for a knockout blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Onerous means heavy as a load or duty to carry.

clue.text: Sighed for an Oxford feature in the South of France

indicators.note: the city's feature is placed inside the French word

parts.note: sud is the French word for south
Oxford is the city of dreaming spires

explanation.surface: Someone sighs over Oxford while living on the Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the South of France' is not the Riviera but the French word SUD, which 'in' puts round SPIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspire is a literary verb for drawing a long breath of longing.

clue.text: Wake here like a bird

parts.note: as means like, as in white as snow
the tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A bird wakes, or a ship's wake is here like a bird's trail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wake' is not waking up but the track a ship leaves behind it in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's wake trails behind the vessel, the direction sailors call aft.
